name: V2 Retail Ltd
title: V2 Retail Ltd - 532867 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: V2 Retail Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR997 crore, with PAT up 70% to INR41.9 crore and store count at 381.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR997 crore (+58% YoY), with reported EBITDA of INR139.5 crore (+60%, 14.0% margin) and PAT of INR41.9 crore (+70%). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was about INR79 crore (~8% margin, +51%) and PAT INR50 crore (+64%). Gross margin eased to 28.6% from 29.5%, which management attributed to Adhik Maas reducing full-price sell-through to 90% from 92%. Store count reached 381 at June 30, 2026 (56 net adds), and management says it has since crossed 400 stores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of at least 50% revenue growth, 8-10% SSSG, 170-200 new stores and 29-30% gross margin.

financial_highlights.change: vs 92% in prior-year Q1 per Q&A

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 381 stores at June 30, 2026 covering ~40.7 lakh sq ft; 57 opened and 1 closed in Q1, net +56. Crossed 400 stores after quarter-end. Stores are mostly standalone, 10,000-12,000 sq ft, in 26 states.

segments.name: New vs mature stores
segments.commentary: New stores run ~34% lower sales per sq ft than mature stores (>2 years old at ~INR1,070-1,100/sq ft); new stores at ~INR730-740/sq ft. New-store SSSG is ~2.3 pts above old stores in Q1. Cohort SPSF cited at 886 vs 925 earlier.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance at least 50% for FY27, unchanged.
SSSG guidance 8-10% for the full year, retained despite Q1 at ~7.5%.
Gross margin guided at 29-30% (earlier 28-30% range), dependent on sell-through.
170-200 store openings planned for FY27; no change in plan despite capex inflation.
Targeting ~50% CAGR growth for the next 2-3 years, per CEO.
Price increase of 4-5% in garment MRPs from Q3 FY27 to offset raw material inflation.
EBITDA margin to be maintained despite the new-store expansion; new stores pay back in 2.5-3 years and break even from their first month.
Funding via internal accruals, release of ~INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases; no QIP planned.
capex_capacity: New store capex has risen ~10% to INR1.22 crore from INR1.1 crore, due to input inflation.
Inventory held ~100 days (earlier 90-100 days target) and creditors ~45-50 days; safety stock raised due to geopolitical tension and to be reduced later.
Inventory for new stores is staged ~2 months ahead, with ~INR100-150 crore tied up per quarter of 50-55 openings.
MOU signed for the next 100 stores; ~15-20 store locations finalised each month based on regional data.
Store-level replenishment cut to 2-3 days of sales cover from 10-12 days, with store back-room space converted into selling area.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is inelastic; kids' wear is ~25% of sales. July-August trends described as in line with plan, but too early to judge given festive shift into Q3.
Adhik Maas (30 days in Q1) and fewer wedding dates weakened Tier 2/3 demand and cut full-price sales to 90%.
Price increase of 4-5% on garment cost from Q3; management says past increases reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.
Repeat customers within first year rose from ~40% to ~55% over three years, per management.
80% of stores face 3-4 other value fashion retailers in the same catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Will price increases be passed on, and what is the volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material inflation to hit from Q3 as H1 orders were placed earlier; a 4-5% rise in garment cost will be passed to consumers. Past price hikes reduced volume slightly but were offset by ASP.

qa_highlights.question: Will the store addition pace slow or need new equity?
qa_highlights.answer: 170-200 openings remain on track with no capex slowdown. Internal accruals, INR150-200 crore from normalising creditor days, and bank limit increases will fund it; no QIP planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Adhik Maas cut full-price sales to 90% from 92%. Guidance remains 29-30% gross margin, dependent on season sell-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new-store productivity gap closing?
qa_highlights.answer: New stores run ~34% below mature stores on SPSF; 10-12 stores are below INR600/sq ft, which management says is too early to judge. Management expects maturity in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are stores appearing in Tier 1 cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said V2 has long operated in Tier 1 (about 11 stores in Delhi NCR) and that Tier 1 is part of the target market.

qa_highlights.question: Customer experience: are NPS or other KPIs tracked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not focus on Google reviews; an NPS link is sent after billing to ~40% of customers as a pilot, with store incentives linked to NPS. AI on CCTV flags long checkout queues.

risks_watch: Gross margin at 28.6% is below the 29-30% guided range; the recovery depends on full-price sell-through in the festive season (Q2-Q3).
New-store productivity is ~34% below mature stores, with 10-12 stores below INR600/sq ft; RK Retail acquisition will consolidate from Q2.
Working capital is inflated by vendor prepayments; cash release depends on creditor days normalising to 45-50 days.
Capex inflation (~10%) and rising rent escalation (12-15% every 3 years) could pressure store economics.
Geopolitical risk is driving higher safety stock and raw-material inflation; the timing of 4-5% price pass-through is a watch item.
Customer experience issues (store-level reviews and checkout queues) could weigh on repeat rates and SSSG.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and store expansion; cautious and deflective on near-term demand, saying it is too early to call July-August trends ahead of the festive quarters. Management gave few numbers on the post-quarter trend and deferred several questions to the next call.
key_quotes: We delivered an amazing 58% year -on-year revenue growth in the first quarter while maintaining healthy returns.
So we need to have that inventory at least 2 months prior to the opening of the store.

adds.what: 170-200 new V2 Retail stores in FY27 (381 stores at June 30, 2026; crossed 400 after quarter-end)
MOU signed for next 100 stores; ~15-20 locations finalised monthly

growth.why: Management reiterated at least 50% FY27 revenue growth backed by 170-200 new store openings (57 opened in Q1 alone, 381 stores at June 30 and 400+ after quarter-end) and an MOU for 100 more stores, though Q1 SSSG of ~7.5% and full-price sales slipping to 90% add some risk to the 8-10% SSSG guide.
